user_input: as a team of 5 agents, upgrade and expand the platform, its info, its features and usability.
title: HarborPath in-place enhancement

assessment_snapshot.intro: The documentation describes HarborPath as an existing bilingual harm-reduction and care-navigation platform with:
bullets: 161,462 JavaScript/TypeScript LOC across 10 visible top-level project directories; the project profile classifies the request as an in-place upgrade of the same platform.
A dependency-free Node.js server and browser-native ES modules, with public directories and care-navigation tools.
Clinical state held in browser RAM only—not URLs, persistent storage, network requests, or logs—and coarse location quantization with local geocoding.
A registered, synchronous Quick Exit reset designed to remain reliable across failures and in-flight work; English/Spanish parity, accessibility, and print parity are explicit guardrails.

PHASE1_HELPERS.md names plain-language variants and answer-specific additions for older-adult, stimulant-use, and co-occurring pathway cards as next possibilities; AI_NAVIGATOR_SPEC.md lists a fully on-device model as a future optional layer.
ARCHITECTURE.md documents stale-result and dataset-freshness metadata for treatment and telehealth directories.

proposed_outcome: Deliver a bounded in-place improvement to existing HarborPath information and usability, preserving current user-facing behavior, dependency-free architecture unless explicitly changed, English/Spanish parity, accessibility and print behavior, identical security headers, RAM-only clinical state, coarse/local location handling, and resilient Quick Exit. Do not introduce clinical or legal claims; any new clinical content must be supported by authoritative primary sources, framed bilingually with limitations, and include appropriate emergency escalation.
